Action Plan:
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
- Initiate migraine-type headache management today with NSAID-first strategy: Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented); continue paracetamol as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented). Note: clinician indicated NSAIDs may be more effective for migraine; paracetamol can be used but may be less effective.
- Address potential triggers and modify lifestyle: advise stress reduction measures; consider taking time off work (one week, self-certification) and explore counselling options (provide link to local service).
- Lifestyle and hydration guidance: encourage 7–8 hours of sleep per night and daily fluid intake of 1.5–2 liters (excluding coffee/tea) to help reduce headache burden.
- Follow-up and safety plan: schedule a follow-up in one week; if symptoms worsen or new red-flag symptoms develop, consider sooner reassessment and possible blood tests; provide danger-signs information link in notes for patient review.

Subjective:
- Chief complaint: New, severe left-sided headache waking the patient at ~5:30 am; ongoing at the visit.
- History of present illness: Acute onset this morning; unilateral left-sided pain, described as very severe; previously had headaches but not this severe; photophobia (light sensitivity) with mild eye soreness; no neck stiffness; no fever; initial dizziness upon waking (resolved); nausea not persistent.
- Temporal pattern: Woke from sleep, currently still present; lying down provides initial relief after onset.
- Exposures/associations: Under significant work stress with late nights for ~2 months; history of anxiety; on sertraline.
- Medications: Sertraline (current); paracetamol taken this morning with little relief (no other meds).
- Allergies: None known.
- Social history: Lives with partner; non-smoker; has a cat; exercises ~3x/week; high workload.
- Family history: No migraines on maternal/paternal side reported; mother with anxiety.
- Review of systems: No fever; no persistent nausea; no vomiting; no focal neurological symptoms described; no suicidal ideation or self-harm thoughts.

Objective:
- Exam performed: None completed in this encounter; clinician notes inability to perform physical exam.
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Focused findings reported by patient: Photophobia present; left-sided predominance; no neck stiffness; no fever; dizziness earlier but resolved; no aura described.
- Investigations: None ordered today.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Headache (likely migraine vs tension-type headache)
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis (from transcript and DDx consistency): 
     - Migraine without aura — High likelihood.
     - Tension-type headache — Medium-High likelihood.
     - Rationale: unilateral left-sided headache with photophobia; stress/anxiety history; relief with lying down; acute onset this morning in a patient with prior headache history.
   - Differential diagnoses (from DDx consistent with transcript):
     - Dehydration-related or sleep-deprivation–related headache; dehydration and sleep disruption discussed as contributing factors.
     - Sertraline-related headache (SSRI-associated) considered but less likely given long-term stability.
     - Other broad differentials (e.g., sinusitis, intracranial process) discussed but not supported by current features (no fever, no neck stiffness, no focal neuro signs).
   - Investigations planned: 
     - None today. If not improving, consider basic labs (e.g., CBC, CRP) and/or further evaluation.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Ibuprofen (first-line for migraine-type headache); dose/route/frequency not documented.
     - Paracetamol can be continued; dose/route/frequency not documented.
     - Lifestyle measures: stress reduction strategies; ensure adequate sleep and hydration.
     - Work modification: consider one week of self-certified time off to reduce trigger exposure.
     - Counseling: referral available; patient encouraged to pursue counselling; provision of local service link.
   - Referrals: Counseling service referral offered; follow-up appointment in 1 week.
   - Additional patient education: Provide patient with information on danger signs of headaches and when to seek urgent care.
   - Contingencies: If symptoms persist or worsen, or if new concerning features develop, reconsider investigations and broader differential; blood tests may be arranged.
